summary: Right-handed tennis serve at ball contact: airborne, racket arm extended high, ball struck well above the head, left arm tucked in, shoulder over shoulder.

cameras.name: net_view
cameras.text: From across the net, telephoto compression, racket strings sharp.

cameras.name: wide_cinema
cameras.text: Wide frame from behind the player, court lines and net ahead, stadium blurred.

rules.why: elbow about 30 deg at contact, nearly straight
shoulder elevation about 111 deg (world-class arm abduction 101 deg)
contact high above the head, about 1.4-1.55 x body height
both feet off the ground at contact (jump about 12 cm)

text.action: a right-handed tennis player hitting a serve at full reach, airborne
text.core: Both feet off the court, legs extended and toes pointed; body rising and tilted so the right shoulder is above the left; right racket arm reaching up almost straight, racket face meeting the ball well above and slightly in front of the head; left arm folded into the chest.
cues: hit up and out at full reach
tossing arm folds in as the racket arm extends
kinetic: racket head motion blur, ball flattened on the strings
hair and shirt lifted by the jump

sources.cite: Jacquier-Bret & Gorce 2024, meta-analysis of tennis serve kinematics (front knee 64.5 +/- 9.7 deg at trophy; shoulder elevation 110.7 +/- 16.9 deg and elbow 30.1 +/- 15.9 deg at contact) - search extract
